elements.quote: Objective: This living systematic review aims to integrate the morphological and tissue-based molecular char­ acterization of oral lesions occurring in individuals infected by COVID-19 (OLICs).
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly identifies the work as a 'living systematic review' and states its aim.

elements.quote: Objective: This living systematic review aims to integrate the morphological and tissue-based molecular char­ acterization of oral lesions occurring in individuals infected by COVID-19 (OLICs).
elements.reason: The abstract provides a clear statement of the main objective/review question.
The abstract does not state the main inclusion or exclusion criteria; such criteria are reported elsewhere (Methods) but not in the abstract text provided.

elements.quote: PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, Ovid, Embase, and LILACS were searched to identify reports on OLICs with morphological and/or tissue-based molecular data.
elements.reason: The abstract lists the information sources searched but does not report when each source was last searched (no search date reported in the abstract).
The abstract does not describe the methods used to assess risk of bias in included studies.
The abstract does not specify the methods used to present and synthesize results (e.g., narrative synthesis, statistical methods) beyond reporting findings.

elements.quote: Results: Four studies reporting five cases were included. Three patients were male, and the mean age of the individuals was 47.6 years.
elements.reason: The abstract reports the number of included studies and cases and summarizes key participant characteristics (sex, mean age).

elements.quote: The most reported anatomical location was the palate (n = 4), whereas ulcers were the most frequent clinical presentation (n = 3). Histopathologically, all cases revealed cell vacuolization and exocytosis in the epithelial layer. In the mesenchymal layer, inflammatory cell infiltrate and thrombi/micro­ vascular thrombosis were observed in three cases. Immunohistochemical reactions were performed in two cases. Both cases were negative for HHV-1, HHV-2, and CMV. One case revealed positivity for SARS-CoV-2 spike protein.
elements.reason: The abstract presents results for main outcomes with counts for findings and number of cases contributing to specific observations.

elements.quote: Results: Four studies reporting five cases were included.
elements.reason: No meta-analysis was conducted or reported in the abstract (only four studies and five cases, with descriptive findings), so reporting a summary estimate and interval is not applicable.

elements.quote: Results: Four studies reporting five cases were included.
elements.reason: The abstract does not report any group comparisons or effect direction; with case reports only, comparative effect direction is not applicable.
The abstract does not briefly summarize important limitations of the included evidence (risk of bias, inconsistency, imprecision).

elements.quote: Conclusions: The pathological characteristics of OLICs are still unspecific. However, with the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic and well-documented new cases, whether OLICs are due to coinfections or has a primary origin can be determined.
elements.reason: The abstract provides a general interpretation of the results and notes implications for future determination of lesion origin.
The abstract does not specify the primary source of funding for the review.
The abstract does not provide the register name and registration number (registration is reported elsewhere in the document but not in the abstract).

No retrieved evidence describes the current state of knowledge or important uncertainties about oral lesions in COVID-19; no introductory or background text providing rationale was provided in the supplied chunks.
No retrieved evidence explains the importance or need for conducting this review; the supplied chunks lack an introduction or rationale section.

elements.quote: Case reports and case series on OLICs confirmed by polymerase chain reaction (PCR) tests and presenting the histopathological report and/or tissue-based molecular characterization (i.e., immunohistochemistry, electron microscopy, immunofluorescence, or PCR) of the lesion were included in this LSR. No restrictions were imposed on the date of pub­ lication, language or geographic region where the study was conducted. Bibliographic reviews, systematic reviews, editorial reviews, meeting/ congress abstracts, experimental studies, in vitro or ex vivo studies, and articles in which it was not possible to access the full text were excluded.
elements.reason: The eligibility criteria specify eligible study designs (case reports and case series), required confirmation (PCR), required outcomes/materials (histopathological report and/or tissue-based molecular characterization), and list excluded study types and access requirements.

elements.quote: The selection was performed in two phases by two authors (L.S.F. and A.L.R.M.). In phase 1, the two authors independently reviewed the titles and abstracts of all references according to the eligibility criteria. If the title or abstract fulfilled the eligibility criteria, the study was incorporated into phase 2. In this phase, the same eligibility criteria were applied to the full text of the articles. Possible disagreements be­ tween the two authors were resolved by a third author (A.C.U.V.) - a senior lecturer in Oral Pathology & Oral Medicine. The final selection was made based on the full text of the publication, ensuring that only studies that did not meet the eligibility criteria were excluded. The calibration of the reviewers was verified by assessing the agreement among the three reviewers (L.S.F., A.L.R.M., and A.C.U.V.) regarding the evaluation of titles/abstracts of the first 50 references retrieved during the searches. A kappa value of 0.93 was achieved, i.e., excellent agree­ ment between reviewers.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly describes the multi-phase selection process, application of eligibility criteria at title/abstract and full-text stages, resolution of disagreements by a third reviewer, and calibration (kappa) — which are the processes used to decide which studies were eligible for inclusion in the synthesis.

elements.quote: In recent systematic reviews (Santos et al., 2021a, 2021b) of oral manifestations in COVID-19 patients, authors reported that oral lesions exhibited miscellaneous clinical aspects, such as ulcers, blisters, macules, and plaques, varying in quantity, color appearance, and anatomical localization. Most patients had oral mucosal injury during the hospitalization period, supporting the hypothesis of coinfections, immunity impairment, or adverse reactions from medications for COVID-19 treatment. In this sense, it is important to consider whether these oral lesions are directly related or secondary to SARS-CoV-2 infection (Santos et al., 2021a, 2021b). ... It has been reported that angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2) is the main host cell receptor for the novel coronavirus, therefore presenting a key role in the entry of the virus into cells (Zou et al., 2020). Considering the oral mucosa tissues as a possible route for SARS-CoV-2 infection, Xu et al. (2020) showed that the expression of ACE2 is highly enriched in the epithelial cells of the tongue, which could then be considered a possible route for coronavirus infection through oral cavity tissues.
